ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows the amplitude-frequency response |H(f)| of an ideal band-pass filter. On the frequency axis, there is a rectangular passband near +f_c, and there is also a symmetric rectangular passband near -f_c; the dashed line marks the passband height as 1, so within the passband |H(f)|=1. Beside the right passband, the bandwidth is labeled as B, and the symmetric left passband also corresponds to bandwidth B. Reasoning: The input is zero-mean Gaussian white noise, whose two-sided power spectral density is n_0/2. The average output noise power is P_out = ∫ S_x(f)|H(f)|^2 df. Only the two passbands contribute, each passband has width B, and |H(f)|^2=1. Therefore P_out = (n_0/2)·B + (n_0/2)·B = (n_0/2)·2B = n_0 B.

method.method_draft: First describe the plot: identify the two rectangular unit-height passbands around ±fc and note that each has bandwidth B. From the text, take the input noise PSD as the two-sided constant n0/2. Apply P_out = ∫ S_x(f)|H(f)|^2 df over the nonzero regions of H(f). The integral covers two intervals of width B with |H|^2=1, giving (n0/2)·2B = n0B.
